newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian FinMin sees '98 budget ready for end-July.
newsitem.headline: Austrian FinMin sees '98 budget ready for end-July.

text.p: Austria's Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said on Friday he would submit the 1998 budget to the council of ministers on July 22, 1997, adding he would also present the outline for the 1999 budget.
"There are still a few details missing but I think we will have an agreed budget by the end of July", Edlinger told Reuters but declined to elaborate.
The remarks came amid crucial negotiations between the government and civil servants, who staged two strikes last month, over job cuts and pension reform.
Edlinger said the federal budget deficit in 1998 will come in between 2.6 and 2.7 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
A consolidation of the budget would continue by cutting expenditures and adjusting revenues, he said.

He reiterated earlier statements that Austria's budget for 1997 was in line with expectations, matching the three percent deficit quota which would qualify Austria for the starting group of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.
Edlinger is scheduled to deliver his budget speech to parliament on September 18, 1997. -- Christian Gutlederer, Vienna Newsroom, +43 1 531 12 275
